title: Upgrade ripple-checker: lightweight customer-aware quality probes on model promotions
creator: Ava Moreno
description:
Motivation: When a model version is promoted in the catalog or a tenant pins a new model, small changes can cause customer-visible quality regressions. We need a lightweight, tenant-aware probing layer ("ripple-checker") that runs targeted, cost-conscious checks immediately after promotions to provide an early warning and enable automatic safe-fail behavior.

What this ticket delivers: a product-level design and rollout plan for an automated, low-cost evaluation sampler that: 1) runs a configurable set of probe queries (tenant-specific plus canonical smoke inputs) against the new version, 2) compares results using lightweight metrics (response correctness, key-slot extraction, embedding similarity, hallucination heuristics), 3) scores impact relative to the baseline model and tenant expectations, and 4) surfaces actionable signals to Console and the rollout orchestration (block/slow/cancel promotion).

Key constraints: keep per-promotion token usage low (target <= 1k tokens per tenant by default), avoid adding tail latency to production traffic, and be conservative in alerting to prevent noisy interrupts to normal rollouts. The system must support both catalog promotions (platform-wide) and tenant-pinned upgrades (customer-scoped), and apply tenant-level thresholds and cost budgets.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc published in Confluence with flow diagrams, sampling strategy, and failure modes
Eval dispatcher API + lightweight sampler prototype exists in staging able to call existing eval harness
Default probe bundle defined (10 canonical smoke inputs + tenant-sampled 20 examples) and config UI wireframe in Console
Automatic gating behavior defined: thresholds, severity buckets, and recommended actions (block/notify/allow with warning)
Cost guard implemented: per-tenant token cap and global budget for catalog promotions
Observability: dashboard with pass/fail rates, delta metrics, and per-tenant impact scoring; alerts created for P0/P1 degradation tiers
notes:
Design should aim for modularity: sampler, comparator, scorer, and policy layers. Start with a conservative comparator (exact-match + BLEU-like + normalized embedding cosine) and iterate to more nuanced checks once baseline noise is understood. Coordinate with Runtime team for non-blocking evaluation routing (shadow/isolated calls) and with Console team for rollout UX.

Privacy: tenant-sampled examples must respect PII handling rules; use token redaction heuristics and optional tenant-provided test sets.

Rollout plan suggestion: 1) internal catalog promotions only (no customer pin) for 2 weeks, 2) opt-in tenants for pinned upgrades, 3) enable auto-gating for high-impact promotions later.

Cost estimate: initial infra and UI work ~5 points; ongoing compute costs expected but controlled by token caps.

Open questions: how to synthesize representative tenant samples for low-traffic tenants; how to map eval signal to percent-of-traffic canary adjustments.
